statement: SharePoint Advanced Management is a separate SharePoint Premium add-on to buy alongside Copilot.

evidence.quote: Microsoft SharePoint Premium – SharePoint Advanced Management (SAM) helps you reduce oversharing and cleanup inactive sites.
As of early 2025, SharePoint Advanced Management is included with your Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

expected: Superseded: SAM is included with Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses (as of early 2025); no separate purchase needed for Copilot customers.

statement: Copilot works across shared, delegate, group and archive mailboxes.

evidence.quote: It isn't available on a user's archive mailbox, group mailboxes, or shared and delegate mailboxes that they have access to.

expected: Answer No: Copilot is supported only on primary mailboxes hosted in Exchange Online. A Yes is a risky commitment.

statement: All Copilot interactions, including web-grounded queries, are covered by the DPA and BAA.

evidence.quote: HIPAA compliance doesn't apply to web search queries as they aren't covered by the DPA and Business Associate Agreement (BAA).

expected: Narrow it: HIPAA support applies to properly configured implementations; web search queries are not covered by the DPA or BAA.

statement: All Copilot processing for EU users, including web search and every model, stays in the EU Data Boundary.

evidence.quote: The EU Data Boundary doesn’t apply to web search queries.
Anthropic models are out of scope for the EU Data Boundary and when available, in-country LLM processing commitments.

expected: Narrow it: Copilot is an EU Data Boundary service for EU customers, but web search queries and Anthropic models are excluded.

statement: Security Copilot is included with Microsoft 365 E5 licenses today.

evidence.quote: In the coming months, Security Copilot will be included with your Microsoft 365 E5 licenses.

expected: Say roadmap: inclusion with E5 is announced for the coming months, not current; answer No today.

statement: Copilot experiences are consolidated under *.cloud.microsoft, so one wildcard is enough.

evidence.quote: Microsoft plans to consolidate Copilot experiences for Microsoft 365 under the `*.cloud.microsoft` domain.

expected: Say planned: consolidation is a plan; today WSS must reach both *.cloud.microsoft and *.office.com and the worldwide Microsoft 365 endpoints must be allowed.

statement: One entry says nothing trains foundation LLMs; the other says optional user feedback trains the foundation LLMs.

evidence.quote: We don't use this feedback to train the foundation LLMs used by Microsoft 365 Copilot.

expected: Flag the conflict; feedback may improve Copilot but is not used to train the foundation LLMs. Correct the feedback entry.

statement: One entry says Copilot Chat needs no additional license; the other says it needs the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on.

evidence.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat uses the web and users can provide organizational data. It doesn't require an additional license.

expected: Flag the conflict; Copilot Chat does not require an additional license (the add-on is for Microsoft 365 Copilot with Graph grounding).

statement: Copilot prompts are subject to Azure OpenAI abuse monitoring with human review (marked Current, last reviewed February 2024).

evidence.quote: While abuse monitoring, which includes human review of content, is available in Azure OpenAI, Microsoft 365 Copilot services have opted out of it.

expected: Mark needs-person / re-review and correct to No: Microsoft 365 Copilot services have opted out of Azure OpenAI abuse monitoring.

statement: Copilot is not yet a covered data residency workload (marked Current, last reviewed December 2023).

evidence.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot was added as a covered workload in the data residency commitments in Microsoft Product Terms on March 1, 2024.

expected: Re-review and supersede: Copilot has been a covered workload (Product Terms, ADR and Multi-Geo) since March 1, 2024; conflicts with the newer residency entry.
